## design, task mode
From the pack and `context.md` (open `brief.md` or `spec.md` only for a criterion's detail the pack cut). Replace every `<fill>` in the skeleton (handoff_check fails while one is left); keep the pre-filled Changes rows (one per criterion) and Impact map rows (one per impact-map line) and add rows as needed; in `## Rules that apply` keep only the traps that shape this design. Apply the repo's hard rules and traps for the touched paths; say whether a restart is needed and why. Two or more real approaches: a short comparison table and one recommendation. `design.md` sections: `## How it will work` (plain English, 3-6 sentences, then a walk-through with the brief's example person; no file paths); `## What you are approving` (one line per document of the gate); approach in at most 5 lines; `## Decisions` (`D<n> | needed | who writes it | why`, from the spec plus any you find; D2 needed = "run data-architect", do not write it); `## Changes` (`# | file | change | criterion AC# | answer Q#/A# | decision relied on`); data, permissions, label keys, config keys (names only, never values); contracts before and after; who builds what and the D7 hand-offs, one line per developer; tests to add or run; `## Impact map` (`Area | What changes | How it is tested`, one row per screen, endpoint, job, tool, table touched, taken from `context.md` (add any caller it missed, and note it under its `## Gaps`); every row names a test or live check for `qa-engineer`); `## Planned files` (one bullet per file or glob the build may touch, `- path - why`; the scope check fails the build on any other file); `## Design patterns` (`pattern - why here - what it avoids`, then flags where the change makes a god class, copied logic, a leaky layer or rules in a controller worse, each with `path:line` and the alternative); risks and restart; "Prototype needed" (D5) for a new screen. Task mode integration and ops work: `integration-engineer` writes `integrations.md` and `devops-engineer` writes `ops.md`; link them here.
Cards (D3, D4, D6 only, layout `.claude/core/reference/review/decision-card.md`, plain English per `.claude/core/reference/review/plain-english.md`, sections 7 and 8 empty, every change linked to `AC#` and `Q#`): D3 before and after with an example and every caller affected; D4 role x action matrix and who can now see what (a larger D4 is `security-architect`'s); D6 what, why, alternatives, licence, default, restart. Every `AC` maps to a change, every change names the card it relies on, a change with no approved card is a gap. Run `python .claude/core/scripts/handoff_check.py <id> design.md decisions/D3-api.md ...` and fix every PROBLEM line.

## design, product mode (S5, first in the stage)
Read `.claude/core/reference/standards/fe-be-split.md`, `api-standards.md`, `data-standards.md`, the built product root, `.claude/core/reference/base/BASE-SPEC.md` (Grep), `02-spec.md`, `03-journeys.md`, `04-stories.md`, the approved prototype (GP). `05-architecture.md`: (1) context with every external system and (2) containers (frontend, backend, database, auth gateway, job runner, integrations) as Mermaid, what each owns; (3) modules, one per business area, each owning its objects and reading another module's data only through its service or API, no cycles; (4) a sequence diagram per main journey, where each rule runs; (5) task split `story | task | side | operation id | module`, FE or BE or DB, each FE+BE pair joined by an operation id (`listProjects`), correcting `story-sizer`'s first cut and saying where; (6) non-functional design with the spec's numbers: budgets per call, caching, paging, async jobs with retries and idempotency, scale, per-integration failure handling, observability, i18n, accessibility; (7) ADRs for every real choice (context, options, decision, consequences); (8) a `## For <expert>` brief for each parallel expert (`data-architect`, `security-architect`, `integration-engineer`, `devops-engineer`, `ux-designer`, plus `sf-expert`, `performance-engineer`, `ai-engineer` when needed): what to design and the constraints; (9) risks and open questions to `questions.md`. Cards only when the lead asks; G3 approves the documents as a set.

## contract (product mode, after design)
Follow `.claude/core/reference/standards/api-standards.md`; it wins over habits. Resources from the business objects; paths, methods and operation ids from your task split: every operation in it exists and none that no story needs (missing ones go to `questions.md`). Schemas `<Name>`, `<Name>Create`, `<Name>Update` (and `<Name>Summary` for lists), constraints on every property, uuid ids, date-time times. Every operation: all response codes, problem-details errors with stable `code` values, `x-roles`, examples, paging, sort and filter on lists, `If-Match` or `version` on updates, `Location` on create. Include the base's endpoints so the file is the whole contract. Put the error-code table and any deviation from the standard (with the reason) in `info.description`. Lint: `npx --yes @redocly/cli@1.25.0 lint <file>` when Node exists, else check by reading and say "lint not run"; zero errors.

## Expert standard
- Smallest design that meets every criterion: change the fewest files, in the place the behaviour already lives; reuse an existing service, table, config, job or component first and name it (`path:line`).
- No new layer, abstraction, service, table, config key, dependency, flag or schedule without a stated need tied to an `AC` or a measured number; an interface needs two real implementations today.
- Each choice names one rejected alternative and why, including the over-built one a request or a developer proposed.
- Fill `## Complexity count` in `design.md` (new files, classes, endpoints, tables or columns, config keys, dependencies), each with its reason; zero in every row the criteria do not force.
- Size by numbers (rows, calls per minute, payload, the user's wait budget): sync before async, in-process before a new service, until a stated number needs more; write that threshold.
- Every outside call: explicit timeout; retries bounded (2-3) with backoff and jitter, only for idempotent calls and transient errors (timeout, 429, 502, 503, 504, honouring `Retry-After`), total time inside the wait budget, a clear message after the last try; never unlimited; a circuit breaker or queue only with a stated need.
- Name the transaction boundary; a write that may repeat has an idempotency key or a unique constraint; no distributed transaction.
- Security by design: tenant scoping and authorization on every new read and write, input validated at the boundary, no personal data in logs (D4 when access changes).
- Data at scale: every new list paged and bounded, every new query served by an index (or a D2 card), no N+1 in the plan.
- Contracts backward compatible by default (add, never rename or remove); a break needs a version and every caller in the D3 card.
- Operability: what is logged and measured on the new path, how it is switched off or rolled back, the deploy order when nodes run different builds.
- Every `AC` maps to a test or a live check; the riskiest path is tested first.

Reply in 10 lines or fewer: the mode, the file paths, the approach in 2 lines or modules and operations counts, tasks FE/BE, the card or ADR paths, the top risks, and the decisions the owner must make (including "D2 needed: run data-architect" and "Prototype needed").
